prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create ONE NEW CORRECTED 3x3 square animation contact sheet for the REVERSE PEC DECK / REAR DELTOID FLY, nine equal SQUARE cells in row-major chronological order. No labels, grid lines, gutters, arrows, numbers or motion trails. Input1 is the approved adult muscular man's identity, naturally colored skin, realistic colored illustration style, black shorts and trainers only; ignore his chest exercise. Input2 identifies a typical gray rear-delt pec-deck machine, chest pad, seat, fixed frame and handles; DO NOT copy its open endpoint into the first pose.
CAMERA IS THE KEY CHANGE: fixed rear/LEFT SIDE three-quarter camera, about55 degrees displaced from directly behind the man, only10 degrees elevated. Man faces diagonally toward IMAGE RIGHT. The near side of his torso, entire NEAR SHOULDER, NEAR ELBOW and NEAR WRIST must be separately visible from the side in the FIRST CELL, so a viewer sees a LONG NEARLY STRAIGHT ARM reaching forward toward the machine. NEVER use the rear-centered high view that makes two bent arms look like a U beside the head. Keep camera, crop, scale, illumination, floor and all fixed machinery exactly identical across all9 cells. Leave enough fixed wide framing for full body and both arms to be visible at maximum lateral spread. Muscular anatomy, realistic hands, same tan skin and materials throughout.
EXECUTION: sit facing the chest pad, sternum stays against it, pelvis seated, feet planted. In EVERY ONE of the nine poses BOTH ELBOWS retain exactly the same small bend, about10–15 degrees off straight (elbow internal angle165–170degrees). Both upper arm and forearm form one long gently bent line. THIS IS NOT AN ELBOW EXTENSION, ROW, SHOULDER PRESS OR PEC FLY.
CELL1: both hands and handles are FORWARD IN FRONT OF THE CHEST at shoulder height, arms reaching forward nearly parallel to floor, near arm visibly extends a full upper-arm-plus-forearm length from its shoulder toward image-right. Near wrist lies a long distance forward of near elbow, near elbow lies forward of shoulder: SHOULDER→ELBOW→WRIST in almost the SAME DIRECTION along that whole line, NO vertically pointing forearm, NO elbow pointing down, NO U posture, NO hands next to the face. Grip handles with neutral wrists. Slight elbow bend already exists and remains constant.
CELLS2–8: open both long nearly-straight arms progressively OUT TO THE SIDES through HORIZONTAL SHOULDER ABDUCTION in small consecutive steps. Imagine a single long rigid radius from each shoulder to hand; elbows do not curl or extend. Near arm arcs OUTWARD TOWARD CAMERA/SIDE while far arm opens to the other side; preserve actual 3D depth, no camera turning. Shoulders remain low and relaxed, trunk/chest/head/feet and hips DO NOT MOVE.
CELL9: arms open approximately in line with torso/shoulders, near arm still has the SAME10–15degree bend as cell1, not farther back than torso. A long-radius arc about shoulders must be obvious through ALL nine cells. No added elbow motion to bring handles back.
MACHINE: two overhead physical pivot housings on a complete fixed crossbeam; two rigid long curved metal levers ending at the shoulder-height grips. Setup first adjusted for REVERSE FLY with forward reach. Each metal lever is ONE UNCHANGING RIGID PIECE that rotates at its fixed pivot to follow the long hand arc, without bending or changing length/width. Chest pad, vertical supporting post, seat, tower and base remain present and fixed, no structural part disappears. Use an opaque covered weight tower (internal weight mechanism hidden) to avoid false static weight plates. Grip contacts stay attached. Nine OPENING keyframes only, no return images. Precise anatomy and clear visible near-side elbow consistency take priority over resemblance to the reference's camera.
